newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures drift upwards, test resistance.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures drift upwards, test resistance.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures nudged up against resistance levels in thin morning trade on Wednesday and seemed poised to build on their gains slightly, brokers said.
"It's rather quiet, but the market seems willing to push things up a bit," a broker said.
Jan Brent bounced as high as $23.02 before settling back to trade at 1245 GMT at $22.92 a barrel, up 18 cents for the day. Intermonth spreads widened with Jan/Feb at +61 cents.
Dec gas oil was up 75 cents at $217.75 a tonne.
The market was bolstered by solid demand for physical cargoes, which was compatible with the drop in crude stocks reported by the American Petroleum Institute on Tuesday, brokers said.
Continued cold weather, particularly in the crucial northeast U.S. market, over the extended U.S. Thanksgiving weekend also buoyed the market, brokers said.
Below normal temperatures are forecast to extend well into next week in both the U.S. and Europe, according to Weather Services Corp.
Brokers did not expect any change at the open of NYMEX, which will be closed on Thursday and Friday for Thanksgiving, because of pre-holdiay anticipation.
"With both Thanksgiving and OPEC, we expect absolutely nothing," a broker said.
The market was closely watching the OPEC meeting in Vienna, which kicks off on Wednesday, but had already factored in an extension of current production quotas into 1997, brokers said.
The first plenary session is scheduled to begin at 1400 GMT and is expected to last until at least Thursday, OPEC Secretary- General Rilwanu Lukman told reporters in Vienna.
